title: Streaming: harden SSE parsing + add onboarding snippet for checklist-linked docs
author: Dana Lo
release_notes:
- TypeScript SDK streaming is more resilient to chunk boundaries / partial SSE frames and common disconnect edge cases.
- New canonical streaming example snippet used by Guided Onboarding checklist docs.
body: Title: Streaming stability improvements + onboarding snippet (checklist docs) Context: We’re seeing avoidable streaming failures during onboarding (SUP-9210 and similar). Common issues: (1) SSE event boundaries split across chunks causing JSON parse errors, (2) network hiccups / server-side idle timeouts leading to premature stream termination without a useful error, (3) Node vs browser differences around ReadableStream + TextDecoder, and (4) example code in docs drifting from the SDK’s recommended usage patterns. This PR hardens streaming behavior in the TS SDK and adds a canonical snippet that the guided onboarding checklist can deep-link to for the “First streaming session” step. Changes (SDK): 1) Robust SSE parsing: - Replaced the naive newline-based parser with a frame accumulator that tolerates arbitrary chunk boundaries (handles partial lines, CRLF, and multi-line `data:` blocks). - Ignores comment/keepalive lines (`: ping`) and tolerates blank lines between frames. - Strictly scopes JSON parsing to `data:` payloads; emits a typed SDK error with the offending frame excerpt on parse failures (redacted/truncated). 2) Better disconnect/error surfacing: - When the stream ends without a terminal event, we now emit `RedwoodStreamError` with `code=STREAM_EARLY_CLOSE` and include request id (if present) + bytes received + last event type. - If the underlying fetch rejects/aborts, we map to `STREAM_ABORTED` vs `NETWORK_ERROR` consistently across browser + Node. 3) AbortController + timeouts: - Added `streamingTimeoutMs` option (default: undefined) that aborts the request if no bytes are received for N ms (useful for proxies / load balancers). - Documented recommended use of AbortController for user-driven cancel. 4) Request IDs for telemetry-friendly correlation: - Plumbs `x-redwood-request-id` from response headers into stream event metadata (where available) so Console/backend validators can correlate a “first streaming session” with gateway logs without relying on prompt content. Changes (examples/docs integration): - Added `examples/onboarding/streaming.ts` as the canonical snippet the docs team links from the checklist. The snippet demonstrates: (a) creating the client with `apiKey`, (b) streaming tokens, (c) abort/cancel, (d) basic retry wrapper around initial request (NOT mid-stream), and (e) logging request id for support/debug. - Added a short README header in the example clarifying environment setup (Node 18+), and explicitly calling out that retries should happen at request boundaries, not by attempting to resume mid-stream. Testing: - Added unit tests for SSE parser with randomized chunk boundaries (including CRLF and multi-line data). - Added a Node integration test using a local mock SSE server that simulates: keepalive pings, chunk splits, and early close. - Verified in: Node 18.19, Node 20.11, Chrome 122. CI: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build` all green. Notes / non-goals: - No automatic mid-stream reconnect/resume in this PR. The API does not currently guarantee resumability, and doing this implicitly could duplicate tokens and break downstream application semantics. - We do not log prompt or completion content; error messages include only truncated parser context without payload by default. Review discussion highlights: - Ibrahim: requested that we avoid default retries during streaming and ensure parse errors don’t accidentally include user content. Addressed by limiting retry example to initial request only and truncating/redacting frame excerpts in errors. - Monica: asked for a clearly copy/pastable snippet aligned with onboarding steps (first request + first streaming). Added the onboarding example and ensured it compiles under `pnpm -C examples/onboarding test` (lightweight smoke). - Amara: requested consistent error codes for analytics; added `STREAM_EARLY_CLOSE`, `STREAM_ABORTED`, `NETWORK_ERROR` and mapped them in one place. Merge: Squash merged to `main`. Follow-ups: - (Not in this PR) Expose an optional `onEvent` hook so Console can later instrument richer streaming events without parsing token text; tracked separately in ENG backlog.
